The deeper worry is traffic burst correlation with shard contention: bursty workloads that trigger cold-starts at scale do so simultaneously across all replicas, meaning the object store (S3, GCS) itself becomes a thundering-herd victim — per-shard checkpoint fetch bandwidth is throttled exactly when every shard is competing for it, amplifying the asymmetry rather than averaging it out. Experts also track the warm-up debt accumulation problem: a partially warmed shard pool that begins serving requests before all KV cache structures, quantization lookup tables, and CUDA graphs are fully materialized will exhibit latency instability for the first N requests even after "warm" status is declared, a failure mode invisible to naive health checks.
